added_failures_note: the reviewed run declared no pytest suite (its manifest baseline_suite and after_suite are empty); its gate logs control.log and measure.log both end EXIT=0 with no failing test id, so no added failures

findings.text: follow-on: neither gate log attests the head revision. control.log and measure.log each begin revision=9a9f2f82aafff0cc56294ddbfefe4b605989bca5, but both files are carried by c2208398, and inside 9a9f2f82 the same logs read revision=4c7dcc79. A reader cannot tie the delivered occupancy_stats.json to the revision that produced it, since epoch() changed between the log's stated revision and the revision that carries the log.

follow-on: only the aggregate reduction is controlled. control() at lines 164-180 exercises aggregate_knee alone, so the piecewise per-request fit (piecewise_break) and the thrash onset (onset) have no synthetic input, and the reported "no break detected" and "onset width 33" are not calibrated against a known-input control as the brief's negative-control requirement asks for the reduction.

follow-on: the recommendation is structurally pinned to 16. lower_supported requires request_break is not None, so proposed is 16 whenever no per-request break is found, regardless of the aggregate knee (width 10, CI 10-16) and of the node's own per-worker yield figures (27.66 tok/s at 13 workers vs 17.35 at 21). The stated basis, that the aggregate knee's upper CI reaching 16 keeps the gate, is therefore never the deciding condition in the observed outcome.

follow-on: receipt_metrics (occupancy_measure.py:371-488) re-derives interval receipt statistics, including a per-request rate from completion over duration, that summarise_receipt_rows already owns; the owner bins by a recorded num_requests_running engine-section row, which the router per-request receipts do not carry, so the reviewed script duplicates part of the capability without extending its owner rather than widening the owner's input contract.

follow-on: the directory now holds occupancy.json, occupancy.png and occupancy_control.json from the pre-existing script this node replaced in place, while the current outputs are occupancy_stats.json and five SVGs; the superseded artifacts are no longer produced by any script and sit beside the current ones under a confusable name.
